mainEntity.name: Is it normal for veneers to feel strange at first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is entirely normal for veneers to feel unfamiliar when they are first fitted. The teeth have been altered in shape and surface, and the mouth's sensory nerves need time to recalibrate. Most patients describe a heightened awareness of their teeth — particularly when eating, speaking, or simply running the tongue across the teeth — during the first week or two. This sensation typically fades as the mouth adapts. If the feeling remains prominent or uncomfortable beyond two to three weeks, a follow-up conversation with your dentist would be worthwhile.

mainEntity.name: Will my speech be affected by veneers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some patients notice a temporary change in speech following veneer placement, particularly with sounds that involve the tongue making contact with the front teeth. This is more commonly reported when multiple veneers have been placed. The tongue adapts quickly to new tooth contours, and for most people, speech returns to normal within a few days to two weeks. Practising speaking or reading aloud at home can help speed up the adjustment. If speech changes persist noticeably beyond two weeks, mentioning this to your dental team is advisable.

mainEntity.name: Can veneers affect the way I bite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Veneers add a thin layer of material to the tooth surface, which can temporarily alter how the upper and lower teeth meet. Your dentist will carefully check and adjust your bite at the fitting appointment, but minor bite awareness in the days following placement is common. This usually settles as the jaw muscles and bite patterns adapt. If the bite feels significantly uneven, causes jaw discomfort, or does not settle within a couple of weeks, contacting your dental team for a bite adjustment is recommended. If your concern is that veneers still feel bulky after the initial adaptation period, this guide on why veneers can feel too thick at first can provide additional context.

mainEntity.name: How do I manage tooth sensitivity after getting veneers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Temporary sensitivity following veneer placement is common and usually manageable. Using a toothpaste formulated for sensitive teeth can help reduce discomfort. Avoid very hot or cold foods and drinks during the first week if these trigger sensitivity. It can also help to avoid highly acidic foods and drinks during the early adjustment period. Sensitivity that persists beyond two to three weeks without improvement should be discussed with your dentist, as this allows them to assess the cause and advise on the most appropriate course of action.

mainEntity.name: How long do dental veneers last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lifespan of veneers depends on the material used, the quality of placement, and how well they are maintained. Porcelain veneers are generally considered more durable and stain-resistant than composite veneers, and with appropriate care and maintenance, many patients find they last ten years or more, though individual longevity varies. Composite veneers tend to have a shorter lifespan and may require polishing or replacement sooner. Good oral hygiene, avoiding habits that place excessive force on the teeth, attending regular dental check-ups, and wearing a nightguard if advised are all factors that can support veneer longevity. Individual outcomes vary and are best discussed with your dental team.

mainEntity.name: When should I contact my dentist after veneer placement?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should contact your dentist if you experience sensitivity, bite discomfort, or speech changes that have not improved within two to four weeks. Additionally, if a veneer feels loose, appears to have shifted, has developed a visible crack or chip, or if you experience gum soreness or swelling around the veneer margins that does not resolve, these are situations that warrant a prompt review. Your dental team is best placed to assess your individual situation and advise accordingly. For general information about what dental check-ups and ongoing care involve, your dental practice can provide personalised guidance.
